claims.evidence: The witness identifies the model as an Xbox One; 'Series 1x' is not a valid Microsoft model name.
The witness saw a home screen and a football game but did not verify the full library or licenses.
FC 26 has not been released; the seller likely means a previous version, and the witness only saw an unidentified football game.

risks.risk: Digital games are tied to a personal account and may be removed after sale.
risks.proof: Screenshot of the 'Full library' showing 'Owned games' or confirmation of account transfer.

risks.risk: Hidden physical damage or heavy scratching under the stickers.
risks.proof: Photos of the console's top surface with all stickers removed.
risks.if_unproven: as having a heavily damaged or 'Grade C' casing.

risks.risk: Internal storage may be the base 500GB rather than 1TB or higher.
risks.proof: Screenshot of the 'Storage' page in the console's System Settings.

risks.risk: The disc drive may be faulty or unable to read discs.
risks.proof: A video clip showing a disc being inserted, recognized, and launched.
risks.if_unproven: as a digital-only console with a broken disc drive.

risks.risk: Controller may have stick drift or unresponsive buttons.
risks.proof: A video of the controller being used with a 'Controller Tester' app showing clean inputs.
risks.if_unproven: as a faulty controller needing replacement.

risks.risk: The Dell monitor may be a low-resolution or old office model.
risks.proof: A photo of the sticker on the back of the monitor showing the model number and manufacture date.

proof_requests: Photo of the back of the Dell monitor showing the model number.
Video of a game disc being inserted and played.
Video of the controller being tested for stick drift in settings.
Photos of the console with stickers removed.
response.reason: The witness has confirmed the item is a functioning Xbox One with a monitor. It will be priced as a base 500GB original Xbox One with a standard monitor, ignoring the seller's claims of non-existent games and confusing model names.
